name: Sarah K. Campbell
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court lacked jurisdiction to realign sentences after a final judgment unless explicitly authorized by statute or rule, emphasizing the importance of finality in criminal judgments.

name: HOLLY KIRBY
description: Dissented, argued that Ms. Hunt has proper standing to challenge the constitutionality of her own voting district because she suffered representational harm from being placed in an unconstitutionally configured district.

name: ROGER A. PAGE
description: Concurred, argued that a positive alert from a drug-sniffing canine can contribute to a finding of probable cause under the totality of the circumstances, despite hemp legalization, and that sufficient facts supported probable cause for the vehicle search.

name: ROBERT L. HOLLOWAY, JR.
description: Concurred, arguing that Public Chapter 182 is constitutional because Article VI, § 5 does not grant exclusive control to district attorneys over collateral review proceedings, which are quasi-civil and not criminal prosecutions, and the legislature has the authority to define the duties of the district attorney.

name: HOLLY KIRBY
description: Concurred, arguing that the right to petition in the Tennessee Constitution is enforceable only against governmental entities and does not create a public policy exception to the employment-at-will doctrine for private employers.

name: SARAH K. CAMPBELL
description: Concurred with the majority opinion, filing a separate concurring opinion.

name: JEFFREY USMAN
description: Concurred, argued that the statute is facially constitutional but unconstitutional as applied to the plaintiffs, and affirmed the award of nominal damages.

name: Sharon G. Lee
description: Concurred, argued that Rule 13 provisions are constitutional as applied, the Petitioner was not unconstitutionally denied appellate review, and he received a full and fair post-conviction hearing.

name: Jeffrey S. Bivins
description: Concurred, argued that to regain suffrage rights in Tennessee, individuals convicted of infamous crimes in other states must comply with both sections 2-19-143(3) and 40-29-202.

name: Sharon G. Lee
description: Dissented, argued that Mr. Falls' voting rights were fully restored by Virginia's clemency under section 2-19-143(3) and he should not be subjected to additional re-enfranchisement requirements of section 40-29-202, as the right to vote is fundamental.

name: Roger A. Page, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the ESA Act only regulates Local Education Agencies (LEAs), which are distinct from county governments, and therefore does not implicate the Home Rule Amendment.

name: Thomas R. Frierson, II, Sp. J.
Sharon G. Lee, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the ESA Act substantially affects the Plaintiffs' local control and sovereignty, thereby implicating the Home Rule Amendment and rendering the Act unconstitutional without local approval.

name: Holly Kirby, J.
description: Dissented with Sharon G. Lee, J.'s opinion.
